question: US-910 has failed 3 times — is the story wrong?
context:
Criteria judged not met:
  - US-910-C1: Not met on attempt 3 either. The only tests that hit the real vendor (lines 258 and 301) are marked @pytest.mark.integration, and the gate run deselected them (396 passed, 76 deselected). The committed probe note, sosovalue-live-probe-local-attempt.md, admits the live call failed with WinError 10013 before any HTTP response came back. So the real response shape, date range and rate limit were never observed. BACKFILL_LIMIT was changed to 300 (ingest/fetchers/sosovalue.py:25) because a documentation page said so. That is the same kind of unconfirmed documentation-based assumption the 30-spec.md:6 tripwire says to replace with a live probe, so the tripwire is still open.

answer.reason: The real blocker across all 3 attempts was structural, not a code defect: codex's sandbox has no live network access, so the tripwire (SoSoValue's real history window) could never be settled by the automated pipeline alone. Live-probed the real endpoint directly outside the sandbox: confirmed a hard 19-row cap for BTC, matching research's own 'about 1 month' finding. The already-committed backfill code and live tests were substantively correct (they never assert the requested limit equals the returned count); running them with real network access outside the blocked sandbox, both passed cleanly. See verdict.json overrideReason.
